You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.

corresponding to one Cypher query — keep the plan as short as the question allows, but make
sure each step is actually answerable by a single query. Revise the plan if a result surprises
you (e.g. an empty result because a field isn't queryable per the schema notes above).

You must query at least one Note passage relevant to the claim/record in question
before you are done — checking policy text alone is not enough to decide Finding vs. No
Finding, someone still has to see what the documentation actually says. Note rows
are reached by traversal (see the schema notes), and the text is long enough that you should
filter by keyword (e.g. `WHERE toLower(e.text) CONTAINS toLower('meniscus')`) rather than
pulling every passage. If you try to stop before querying any Note, you'll be
stopped and asked to check the record first.

Whenever you query Note (or its Fact rows), always RETURN its citation metadata
alongside the text — document/file name, title or note_type, and page_no/printed_page (or
page_start/page_end) — not just the text field alone. The judgment step that reads your
transcript afterward has to cite an exact document/section/page for every passage it relies

Cypher literal strings break on an unescaped apostrophe (e.g. `CONTAINS 'patient's history'`
is a syntax error, not a match) — pick a keyword without an apostrophe, or escape it as `\'`,

If a more specific tool is available for a lookup (check its description), prefer it over

you do here.

[[NAME-0005]] is a 56-year-old man without significant past medical history who was involved in a high-speed motor vehicle collision as

was found unresponsive at the scene. EMS assessment on arrival documented GCS 8 with tachycardia (HR 130) and hypotension (SBP

[[NAME-0005]] presented as a Level 1 trauma activation following a high-speed motor vehicle collision with ejection resulting in severe

embolization of a bleeding right internal iliac branch. The course was complicated by right hemopneumothorax requiring tube

profound ICU-acquired weakness. Post-splenectomy pneumococcal, meningococcal, and Haemophilus influenzae vaccines were
administered. Extubation was successful on ICU day 9 with brief VAP requiring aggressive pulmonary toileting rather than reintubation.

non-weight-bearing precautions on the right lower extremity.

Norepinephrine (Levophed)
Purpose Raises blood pressure when the body is in shock.
Dose & Route Titrated via IV infusion to maintain blood pressure.
Side Effects Decreased blood flow to hands/feet; irregular heartbeat.
Monitoring Continuous blood pressure and heart rate monitoring.
Teach-Back Family verbalized understanding that the medicine keeps blood pressure safe.
Vancomycin
Purpose Antibiotic to treat the blood infection (sepsis) and potential MRSA.
Dose & Route Individualized IV dosing based on kidney function and blood levels.
Side Effects Kidney injury (monitored daily); rash if given too fast (Red Man Syndrome).
Monitoring Daily labs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes.
Teach-Back Family able to state purpose; instructed to report rash or skin flushing.
Piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn)
Purpose Broad-spectrum antibiotic targeting pneumonia and gram-negative bacteria.
Dose & Route 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, extended infusion over 3 hours.
Side Effects Diarrhea; low potassium; allergic reaction (report rash immediately).
Monitoring Renal function, electrolytes daily.
Teach-Back Teach-back deferred - patient sedated. Education provided to son.
Pantoprazole (Protonix)
Purpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.
Dose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.
Side Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.
Monitoring Magnesium levels weekly; discontinue at discharge if no indication.
Teach-Back Patient verbalized that medication protects the stomach.
Enoxaparin (Lovenox)
Purpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.
Dose & Route Prophylactic dose; adjusted if active clot is confirmed.
Side Effects Bruising at injection site; bleeding (report blood in urine/stool).
Monitoring Daily CBC; watch for signs of bleeding.
Teach-Back Son acknowledged understanding of clot-prevention purpose and verbalized when to call

Insulin infusion / Sliding scale
Purpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.
Dose & Route IV infusion titrated to glucose 140-180 mg/dL; transitioned to SC at recovery.
Side Effects
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.
Monitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.
Teach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.
Amiodarone
Purpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).
Dose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.
Side Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use
sunscreen.
Monitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.
Teach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials
provided.

Purpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).

Side Effects Increased bleeding risk - avoid NSAIDs, aspirin without physician approval.

result.system_note: What was billed: Position 1 billed as S36.020A (Contusion of spleen). The claim omitted J18.1 (lobar pneumonia) and includes R57.01 (cardiogenic shock). What the medical record documents: the treating physician (CDI query response) designated J18.1 (lobar pneumonia) as the PRINCIPAL diagnosis and stated the pneumonia "drove the septic cascade" (Principal Diagnosis Clarification, Clinical Documentation Improvement Queries, pp.158-240). The admission H&P and imaging document Grade IV splenic laceration with hemorrhagic (traumatic) shock and the need for emergent splenectomy and IR embolization (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, pp.242-475; Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Trauma Panscan, p.117). The Discharge/Transfer Summary documents ventilator-associated pneumonia due to MSSA and notes extubation on ICU day 9 and transfer to an acute inpatient rehabilitation facility (Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp.859-860). Nephrology specifically documents rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI with peak CK 12,400 and creatinine 2.4 and states "Adequate urine output with aggressive hydration; no RRT indication" (Nephrology Consultation, Chart Notes, p.137). Why this is a Finding: (1) Principal-sequencing - CDI/physician attestation names J18.1 (lobar pneumonia) as the principal diagnosis and instructs septic shock/ARDS be coded as secondary; the claim instead lists a splenic contusion (S36.020A) in principal position. The physician-selected principal diagnosis is authoritative for sequencing (Principal Diagnosis Clarification, Clinical Documentation Improvement Queries, pp.158-240). (2) Missing principal diagnosis - J18.1 is documented in the Problem List and the CDI clarification as principal but is not present in the billed diagnosis position 1. (3) Unsupported/incorrect diagnosis - R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) is billed but the contemporaneous H&P documents hemorrhagic/traumatic shock from splenic hemorrhage (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, pp.242-475) and the record contains no documentation supporting a cardiogenic etiology (no diagnostic data supporting cardiogenic shock; troponin noted negative in H&P labs). The record does document traumatic/hemorrhagic shock (T79.4XXA) and septic shock as in-hospital complications. Recommended correction: re-sequence the claim so principal diagnosis = J18.1 (lobar pneumonia), remove R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) or replace it with the documented shock etiology (traumatic/hemorrhagic or septic shock) supported by notes, and revise the splenic diagnosis coding to reflect the documented Grade IV splenic laceration (documentation: H&P and CT Panscan) rather than a contusion. All listed procedures (intubation, splenectomy, IR embolization, chest tube, pelvic external fixation, femur IM nailing, transfusion, central infusion device, >96-hour ventilation) are supported by the record and may remain. Evidence (document/section/pages cited) used in this determination is provided below.
